recall.note: a blind pattern counts as found when it is anywhere in the census detector set of its item (needs, tokens or plumbing), not necessarily on the same nodes

gaps.fragment: Browser microphone audio (24 kHz int16 chunks) streamed over a WebSocket; server-side voice activity detection decides turn ends
gaps.why: realtime audio duplex stream with model/server-chosen turn boundaries; L0 stream is a bounded batch consumer and has no audio/turn-detection construct

gaps.fragment: transfers to the FAQ or seat-booking agent ... transfers back to triage if it cannot answer
gaps.why: agent-to-agent handoff that keeps the live session conversation (the refused full-history handoff); P46 typed-tool rewrite changes the feature

gaps.fragment: Chat model with the tool list bound and a system prompt carrying the current time
gaps.why: minor: wall-clock injected into the prompt is an input the solver does not declare (would be an L3 binding)

gaps.fragment: UI input widget ui_button / ui_slider / ui_switch / ui_dropdown (33 ui_* nodes); ui_text; ui_gauge
gaps.why: long-lived dashboard widget state is the refused interactive dashboard state

gaps.fragment: device listener (29 nodes) ... set properties / device function / start-virtual-device / generate-event
gaps.why: simulated-device event bus with node-level context state; closest is trigger.event + state but the elevator logic sits in 19 function nodes (opaque code)

gaps.fragment: Code predicates over the run context decide which language tools the model sees
gaps.why: minor: a per-run tool allow-list computed by code from context; L0 agent.tools is a static literal list (allowed, but the dynamic form is not a stated construct)

gaps.fragment: Repeats while the result still holds interruptions
gaps.why: minor: bounded repeat of interrupt-resume needs a literal cap (not stated in the example)

gaps.fragment: 26 http in endpoints (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) plus 28 manual inject test triggers in one flow
gaps.why: minor: one flow hosting 26 independent webhook routes; L0 trigger.webhook is one trigger per envelope, so it decomposes into 26 envelopes (nothing is lost, but it is a bundle not a workflow)

gaps.fragment: (bypassed) nodes: CLIPLoader, UNETLoader, LoraLoaderModelOnly, KSamplerAdvanced, SaveVideo ... (bypassed)
gaps.why: minor: a static per-graph enable/disable of a whole branch (fast vs slow variant) baked into the template; maps to a build-time choice, not a runtime construct

gaps.fragment: any other answer re-runs the search agent with its message history and a request for another flight
gaps.why: minor: re-entering the same agent with its own accumulated message history across turns; closest is session memory (P43), not stated as a construct for a solver

gaps.fragment: ha.action.repeat.while (hold-to-ramp volume loops, 2 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: the loop runs while an external button state holds, with no literal cap; L0 refuses an unbounded while, so a cap must be added (representable, but not as written)

gaps.fragment: ha.action.!input (24 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: blueprint inputs that let the installer supply the action list per button; P57 caller-supplied action list covers it

gaps.fragment: Link 1: keep only numeric values with their metric names, one 'value: metric' line each
gaps.why: minor: hand-offs are free text lines, not typed; the library would need a schema for each link (L0 allows it; the example does not carry it)

gaps.fragment: New Agent per task from the model-written spec: tool subset from the parent registry, optional provider and settings, optional prompt
gaps.why: the parent model writes per-task model/provider/system prompt; L0 only allows model ids from policy/models.json and a plan fragment over call/judge/map, so a model-chosen provider must be narrowed to a tier enum (representable only after narrowing)

gaps.fragment: A scheduler runs ready tasks on a thread pool by priority
gaps.why: minor: priority-ordered dependency scheduling of planned tasks; L0 map/wide have concurrency but no priority queue

gaps.fragment: persists it as JSON ... reloaded by a file watcher
gaps.why: minor: durable workflow store with a file watcher is the host's state, not a construct

gaps.fragment: outputParserAutofixing (5 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: a second model call repairs malformed structured output; this is judge + code check + bounded retry (P20), nothing new

gaps.fragment: slack sendAndWait (2 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: human reply used as free-text edits then re-fed to a model; ask returns untrusted data, OK

gaps.fragment: number_random (9 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: random draws decide game outcomes; a solver's step is pure and L0 has no randomness/clock input (would be an L3 binding passed in as input)

gaps.fragment: ui_text (41 nodes)
gaps.why: 41 ui_text widgets are display-only outputs of the fetched GivEnergy API values (no ui_button/slider/switch inputs); the widget-count criterion would refuse it as dashboard state, but it is inject, HTTP GET, function parse, switch, display, i.e. a status poller, so I read it as explained (output display is done / an L3 notify binding)

gaps.fragment: environment=review-docs/mr-${CI_MERGE_REQ…; stop env
gaps.why: minor: review-app environment with an on_stop teardown run later (deferred compensation tied to an environment lifetime); closest L0 are finally (22) and compensate (23, N)

gaps.fragment: resource_group
gaps.why: minor: mutual exclusion across pipelines; admission (28, N) covers overlapping runs of one workflow, not a named cross-pipeline lock

gaps.fragment: The coordinator writes role, system message and description for a new single-agent worker with default tools, which joins the live roster and starts.
gaps.why: create_worker lets the model define a new agent (role, system prompt, tool set) at run time; L0 has a fixed agent construct with static tools and refuses model-chosen tools and self-modification, so this recovery branch has no construct

gaps.fragment: A model picks retry, replan, reassign, decompose or create_worker, limited to the enabled list; at most 3 failures per task
gaps.why: the strategy choice is a judged enum (fine), but replan and decompose re-enter the planner after execution started, an unbounded-looking plan loop that needs a literal cap; only the cap is missing

gaps.fragment: Handoff is a tool the model calls; all agents continue one chat memory, and their tools write a state dictionary the caller reads at the end.
gaps.why: model-chosen hand-off between agents over one shared conversation is exactly the refused full-history handoff, and the shared state dict is a shared mutable scratchpad (rewritten as wide with a typed reduce, which loses the shared chat memory)

gaps.fragment: documentpicker_open (17) / documentpicker_save (14)
gaps.why: minor: account and channel records are kept in files read and written across runs; this is cross-run state (L0 state is N, designed not built)

gaps.fragment: number_random (16 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: random draws decide game outcomes; no randomness input in a pure solver step (L3 binding)

gaps.fragment: documentpicker_open (14) / documentpicker_save (26)
gaps.why: minor: per-user economy data persisted in files across runs, i.e. cross-run state (L0 state is N)

gaps.fragment: documentDefaultDataLoader / textSplitterRecursiveCharacterTextSplitter / embeddingsGoogleGemini / vectorStoreSupabase mode=insert
gaps.why: minor: the ingestion half of RAG (split, embed, upsert into an index, delete on request) has no pattern; P06 covers only retrieve-then-generate. It composes from map + effect but is not a stated idiom

gaps.fragment: wait resume=timeInterval then blotato get then if, looping back to the wait (3 loops)
gaps.why: minor: poll-until-published loops show no attempt cap or timeout in the graph; L0 requires a literal cap (P21 has TIMEOUT_MS), so one must be added

gaps.fragment: checkpoint tune_predictions_based_on_threshold / checkpoint mosaic_count
gaps.why: minor: Snakemake checkpoint re-evaluates the DAG after the job, so the set of per-cell downstream jobs depends on its output; this is a map over a run-time list (P12), not P31 checkpoint-resume (a name collision)

gaps.fragment: Info ... whose parameter schema is the caller-supplied extraction schema
gaps.why: minor: the output schema arrives as run-time input; L0 judge/agent schemas are literals chosen at compile time, so a caller-supplied schema needs the schema slot filled from input (allowed type, but dynamic)

gaps.fragment: its text deltas are read one by one while the model is still generating
gaps.why: incremental consumption of a model's token stream while it generates; L0 judge/agent return a whole typed result, and stream (30) is a bounded input consumer, not an output-token stream

gaps.fragment: Every 300 characters ... starts a background guardrail check on the text so far ... If a check fails the stream loop breaks early
gaps.why: periodic partial-output checks and cancelling an in-flight generation on a tripwire have no construct (P48 covers a parallel check aborting a whole output, not mid-stream cancellation); a post-hoc check of the full text is a different workflow

gaps.fragment: ha.action.repeat.until (20 nodes); ha.action.wait_for_trigger (44 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: until-loops and waits for an external state change show no literal cap or timeout in the graph; L0 requires both (representable once added)

gaps.fragment: Delay (templated/input) (87 nodes)
gaps.why: minor: delays whose duration is a user input or template; wait.delay is stated with a fixed delayMs and a 1 hour cap

gaps.fragment: Non-empty feedback loops back to drafting; empty feedback goes to final_result
gaps.why: minor: the draft loop ends only when the person accepts, with no cap; L0 requires a literal cap on every loop, so a max-rounds bound has to be added
